    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus request and response transaction",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Merged Into": "",

      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",

      "Candidate Name": "Bus response acknowledge and error",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error is tied to a constant, so Bus handshake copies excludes them as independent information."
    },

      "Candidate Name": "CPU interrupt output as a separate status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",

    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "GPIO register read-back word",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The read-back word only exposes the underlying GPIO data and settings, so Register read-back treats it as an exit of those concepts rather than an independent asset."

      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset controls",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the unit, and the Clocks and resets rule bars them as conceptual assets."

      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "GPIO_NUM only fixes the build-time width and cannot be changed or withheld at run time, so Build-time values excludes it."
    }
  ],

conceptual assets.information: The sampled values presented on the GPIO input pins, on which software reads and interrupt detection depend.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The input may contain sensitive external data and the unit exposes the sampled value through bus_rsp_o.data at line 83; its integrity matters because gpio_i is sampled into the unit at line 103 and the sample drives reads and interrupt detection.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the input through a bus read or alter the GPIO input so that software receives false data and interrupt detection uses the wrong state.

conceptual assets.information: The output values programmed for the GPIO pins, on which the external GPIO function and software read-back depend.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The output setting is modifiable by bus write data at line 74 and drives gpio_o at line 112, so an unauthorized modification can change the externally visible GPIO behavior.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a bus write selecting the output register and change the GPIO pins to an unintended value.

conceptual assets.information: The per-pin trigger type and polarity configuration that determines whether GPIO levels or transitions generate interrupt triggers.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Bus writes modify irq_typ and irq_pol at lines 75-76, while those settings select the trigger behavior at lines 123-128; changing them can cause missed or spurious interrupts.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could rewrite the trigger type or polarity so required GPIO interrupts are suppressed or false interrupts are generated.

conceptual assets.information: The per-pin enable setting that permits detected GPIO triggers to become pending interrupts.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The enable setting is written from bus_req_i.data at line 77 and gates pending interrupt formation at line 141, so it can alter or block interrupt delivery.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could clear or alter the enable bits through a bus write, preventing required GPIO interrupts from reaching the CPU.

conceptual assets.information: The internally accumulated per-pin pending interrupt state, on which the CPU interrupt output and interrupt-status reads depend; no unit port carries this state into the unit because it is generated internally.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The pending state is updated by trigger, enable, and clear control at line 141 and is observable through bus_rsp_o.data and cpu_irq_o at lines 88 and 142, so unauthorized changes can corrupt or suppress interrupt reporting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could clear or corrupt pending bits so the CPU misses a required interrupt, or cause software to observe a false pending interrupt.

conceptual assets.information: The derived per-pin event indicating that the configured GPIO level or transition should raise an interrupt; pending-interrupt behavior depends on this event.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The event is computed from sampled GPIO values and the trigger configuration at lines 125-129, and modifying that result can create false interrupts or prevent required events from reaching irq_pend.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the trigger computation or its inputs so a GPIO event is falsely reported or a real event is never recorded.

conceptual assets.information: The per-pin clear mask written by software that determines whether existing pending interrupts are retained or cleared; it is a transient internal control with no direct read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The clear control is loaded from bus_req_i.data at line 78 and participates in the pending-state update at line 141, allowing a bus write to clear interrupt state and block interrupt delivery.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a clear mask that removes pending interrupts before the CPU services them.
